title: Harbour, last light
note: A small fishing harbour at sunset. Oil on a warm toned canvas: brushed sky, knife-laid water, thick lights.

under.note: flat opaque colour under a shape

paint.note: the working paint: stays wet and melts a little into what is wet

soft.note: for the sky: wetter, melts more

firm.note: clean paint that lies on top

dark.note: darks with gloss, so that their relief shows

slab.note: for the knife in the water: the knife gives it 2.4 times this body

drag.note: paint dragged thin with the knife: it breaks over the ridges under it

impasto.note: thick clean paint for the lights

touch.note: a small square brush set down once

steps.name: Lay-in
steps.note: On a warm sienna ground, the big areas thinly in their own colours: nothing later has to cover bare canvas.

steps.name: Sky
steps.note: Brushed wet into wet with a broad bristle, from violet overhead through rose to orange and yellow over the far shore.

steps.name: Clouds
steps.note: The cloud bodies in cool violet, their undersides turned to the sun in rose and orange, smaller touches worked into the wet sky.

steps.name: Sky lights
steps.note: Thick clean paint put down last and left alone: lit cloud edges, the glow, the sun itself.

steps.name: Far shore
steps.note: A low headland across the water, violet against the light, warmer where the sun goes down behind it.

steps.name: Water, brushed
steps.note: The whole harbour first with a bristle brush: the sky upside down, darker and cooler toward us.

steps.name: Quay and houses
steps.note: A stone pier with a row of houses: fronts in shadow, gable ends and the quay itself in the last sun.

steps.name: Water, knife
steps.note: Slabs laid flat with the palette knife over the brushed water, small and close far off, long and thick near us.

steps.name: Reflections of the quay
steps.note: Wall, houses and lit windows upside down in the water, broken into bars that slide apart as they come nearer.

steps.name: The sun on the water
steps.note: The brightest paint in the picture, thick from the knife: a broken path of light from the far shore to the bottom edge, and stray glints.

steps.name: The far boat
steps.note: Its reflection with the knife, then hull, rails, mast and the furled sail.

steps.name: The cream boat
steps.note: Its reflection with the knife, then hull, rails, mast and the furled sail.

steps.name: The dark boat
steps.note: Its reflection with the knife, then hull, rails, mast and the furled sail.

steps.name: The green boat
steps.note: Its reflection with the knife, then hull, rails, mast and the furled sail.

steps.name: Posts, buoys and lines
steps.note: Mooring posts near us, a buoy or two, the lines that hold the boats, a few gulls.
